report.incident_title: API gateway p99 latency and 504s spiking
report.summary: The 504s and p99 spike are a downstream cascade triggered by the catalog-svc feature flag pdp_cache_include_reviews (0% -> 100% at 18:30Z, growth-team). Cached product:pdp entries grew from ~4.1 KB to ~38 KB. Redis (maxmemory 8 GB, allkeys-lru) filled up at ~19:05, began evicting ~5,000 keys/s, and the hit ratio fell from 0.94 to ~0.40. Cache misses went to catalog-db, which runs a reviews SELECT that took 1.8 to 4.6 s. catalog-db CPU rose to ~98%, catalog-svc's DB pool saturated (40 connections, 312 waiting), and gateway upstream timeouts to catalog-svc produced the 504s. The gateway itself is healthy (CPU 26-31%, falling). Scaling the gateway would push more requests into the saturated path and would not fix the incident.
report.root_cause: Feature flag pdp_cache_include_reviews was ramped to 100% at 18:30Z, so PDP cache entries embed the latest 200 reviews. This inflated cached values roughly 9x. Redis reached its 8 GB maxmemory at ~19:05Z, and allkeys-lru eviction collapsed the hit ratio to ~0.40. Cache misses then hit catalog-db's uncached reviews query, which saturated the DB (CPU ~98%) and the catalog-svc connection pool. Gateway upstream timeouts to catalog-svc produced the 504s and the p99 at the 5 s ceiling.

hypotheses.statement: The pdp_cache_include_reviews flag (18:30Z) inflated PDP cache entries, which exhausted Redis memory and triggered eviction and a hit-ratio collapse. The resulting DB overload on catalog-db caused catalog-svc pool exhaustion and gateway timeouts.

facts.text: feature_flag change at 18:30Z on catalog-svc: pdp_cache_include_reviews 0% -> 100%; details say cache entries now embed the latest 200 reviews.
redis avg_value_size_bytes for product:pdp:* rose from ~4.1 KB (18:25) to ~12.8 KB (18:35), ~21.5 KB (18:40), and ~38.4 KB by 19:00, then flat.

redis used_memory_pct climbed 63% (18:30) to 96% (19:00), and 100% from 19:05. evicted_keys_per_sec went from 0 to 1,200 at 19:05 and ~5,000 thereafter. hit_ratio fell 0.94 (19:00) -> 0.71 (19:05) -> 0.43 (19:10) -> ~0.40.
redis WARN 19:05:12: 'maxmemory reached (8gb); evicting keys with allkeys-lru'.
catalog-svc WARN 19:06:40: 'cache miss product:pdp:88123 -> loading from catalog-db (with reviews)'.
catalog-db WARN 19:09:02: 'duration: 1840 ms statement: SELECT r.* FROM product_reviews r WHERE r.product_id = $1 ORDER BY r.created_at DESC' (the logged statement shows no LIMIT).
catalog-svc ERROR 19:10:15: 'db pool wait exceeded 2000ms (pool=40, waiting=312)'.
catalog-svc latency_p99: 85-106 ms (18:00-19:00), rising from 18:30; 900 ms at 19:05; 4200 ms at 19:10; 5000 ms (ceiling) from 19:15.

Sample error trace t-c03-slow-1 (19:15:20): gateway GET /products/{id} 5000 ms 'upstream timeout'; catalog-svc getProductPage 4990 ms; redis GET product:pdp:77410 1 ms miss; catalog-db SELECT product_reviews 4600 ms.

assumptions: The flag change is the only change to cached value size. Confirming requires checking the cache-write path or per-key payload.
Cached PDP keys carry a long or no TTL, so they will not expire quickly on their own.

hypotheses.statement: The 17:50Z TLS cipher-suite change on api-gateway (security-team) caused the latency and 504s.

facts.text: api-gateway latency_p99 stayed at 138-145 ms from 18:00 to 19:00, after the 17:50 change; it only moved at 19:05. http_504_rate was 0.0% from 18:00 to 19:00.
No TLS handshake or cipher errors in api-gateway logs from 17:45 to 19:40. The only ERROR is the 19:11:50 upstream timeout to catalog-svc.

hypotheses.statement: The gateway is capacity-constrained (the reporter's hypothesis), so scaling it would fix the 504s.

facts.text: api-gateway cpu_utilization was 26-31% during the incident, against a 30-32% baseline before it. CPU fell as errors rose.
Gateway errors are upstream timeouts to catalog-svc, and catalog-svc's DB pool has 312 waiters. More gateway replicas would send more requests into the same saturated path.

hypotheses.statement: Organic traffic growth or an independent catalog-db fault (not cache-driven) caused the DB saturation.

facts.text: catalog-db CPU rose gradually from 38% (18:00) to 45% (19:00) before the 19:05 step.
The DB WARN is the reviews SELECT that follows cache misses. No DB-side change or infra event was logged.
get_infra_events returned no events since 17:00Z, and get_changes returned no changes for redis-cache.

assumptions: No request-rate series was available to rule traffic growth in or out. This needs gateway/catalog RPS and a per-endpoint breakdown.

corrective_actions.action: Roll back feature flag pdp_cache_include_reviews to 0% on catalog-svc now. Coordinate with growth-team, who own the flag.
corrective_actions.rationale: The 18:30Z flag change is the trigger. Its timing matches the cache-size growth, the eviction onset and the DB overload. Rollback is the fastest reversal.

corrective_actions.action: Purge or expire the oversized product:pdp:* keys in redis-cache so the cache repopulates at ~4 KB. Watch the hit ratio recover and catalog-db CPU fall. Shed or rate-limit catalog-db load while the cache refills.
corrective_actions.rationale: Entries already written at ~38 KB keep memory full and keep evicting useful keys until they are overwritten or expire. TTL is unverified.

corrective_actions.action: Do not scale api-gateway. Relieve catalog-svc/catalog-db only if still needed after the cache recovers.
corrective_actions.rationale: Gateway CPU is 26-31% and the bottleneck is catalog-db and the catalog-svc pool.

corrective_actions.action: Redesign the PDP cache so reviews are not embedded in product:pdp entries. Cache reviews separately with a size cap, or fetch them at render time. Enforce value-size caps.
corrective_actions.rationale: The ~9x payload growth exhausted Redis memory. Keeping cached blobs small preserves the hit ratio.

corrective_actions.action: Optimise the reviews query on catalog-db: add an index on product_reviews(product_id, created_at), enforce a LIMIT, and verify with EXPLAIN.
corrective_actions.rationale: The logged reviews SELECT took 1.8-4.6 s under load and drove DB CPU to ~98%. The logged statement shows no LIMIT, though logging may have truncated it.

corrective_actions.action: Require load and memory testing plus a staged canary before ramping any flag that changes cache value size. Give the product cache its own Redis instance or keyspace budget so it cannot evict unrelated keys.
corrective_actions.rationale: The flag went from 0% to 100% in one step with no guardrail on payload size or memory headroom.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on redis used_memory_pct > 80%, sustained evicted_keys_per_sec > 0, hit ratio < 0.8, avg value size > 2x jump, and catalog-svc DB pool wait. Add a rate-of-change alert on flag-driven payload growth.
corrective_actions.rationale: Memory exhaustion and the hit-ratio drop ran for ~35 minutes (18:30-19:05) before the 504s, and no alert fired on them.

missing_data: Request rate (RPS) for api-gateway, catalog-svc and catalog-db. Needed to rule out organic traffic growth.
Redis TTL policy for product:pdp:* keys and the exact cache-write code path. Needed to estimate how long oversized keys persist after rollback.
Runtime flag-evaluation logs from catalog-svc showing per-request flag state. No startup or config lines came back for catalog-svc.
Gateway p99 is capped at 5000 ms in the metrics, so the true latency tail is not visible.
Full catalog-db query text (the logged statement shows no LIMIT) and its EXPLAIN plan.
The runbook and past-incident searches returned nothing for redis maxmemory or PDP cache, so no runbook guidance applies.
security_findings: No security findings. The 17:50Z TLS cipher change was reviewed and ruled out as a cause; it produced no errors or latency change in the gateway data.
questions_for_human: Has growth-team been paged, and can the pdp_cache_include_reviews flag be rolled back now? Who owns the rollback decision for this SEV1?
What is the TTL on product:pdp:* keys? If it is long, is a targeted purge of that keyspace acceptable during the incident?
Was the reviews query on catalog-db already in use at 0% (so not newly added), or was it introduced by the flag?
